evidence_quotes: 38 earthquakes were recorded globally over the 7-day period
daily counts climbed from 4–5 events early on to a peak of 9 events on Feb 14
Magnitudes ranged from M4.0 to M5.7, with an average of M4.56
Tobelo, Indonesia was the week's most active hotspot, logging 5 events including the largest quake of the period (M5.7 on Feb 14)
a M4.8 near Tual, Indonesia struck at just 2 km depth
a M5.2 off Honshu, Japan at 2.7 km
No tsunami warnings were triggered across any of the 38 events
Banda Sea (M5.6, 177 km) and Kuril Islands (M5.3, 113 km)
Mohr, Iran sequence (3 events including a M4.9 at shallow depth)
criticisms: The report refers to 'Kuril Islands' when the digest lists the place as 'Kuril'sk, Russia' — a minor but technically imprecise place name substitution, though the region is recognizable.
The Banda Sea depth is cited as '177 km' — the digest shows 176.6 km, which is a minor rounding that is acceptable but slightly imprecise.

The phrase 'can sometimes precede larger ruptures' in the Tobelo section edges toward predictive framing, though it is hedged with 'sometimes' and does not specify a date, location, or magnitude, so it remains within acceptable monitoring language.

The report states 'daily counts climbed from 4–5 events early on' — the digest shows Feb 9 had 5 and Feb 10 had 4, which is accurate, but Feb 11 had only 2, so the characterization of a smooth climb is slightly misleading, though not a fabricated number.
